coverage_summary: Reviewed all 8 trajectories. The opaque GIN, ESM-2, and placeholder-fusion boundaries are justified. Several documented dataset branches, preprocessing steps, and split conditions are missing or collapsed.

findings.detail: The PubChemQA preparation is represented as one opaque boundary even though the paper documents ordered filtering and graph-generation operations. This loses source-supported text filtering and its order.

evidence.quote: We remove molecules that cannot be processed by RDKit [Landrum et al., 2021] to generate 2D molecular graphs. We also remove texts with less than 4 words, and crops descriptions with more than 256 words.

findings.required_change: Preserve the opaque RDKit graph-generation boundary if needed, while adding separate documented filtering calls or boundaries for processability, short-text removal, and long-description cropping, with their stated order and intermediate nodes.

findings.detail: The UniProtQA alignment route starts from an undifferentiated UniProtQA protein/query node and does not represent the documented random split or the restriction of multimodal fine-tuning to the training split.

evidence.quote: The data was randomly divided into training, validation, and test sets at a ratio of 8 : 1 : 1 . The multi-modal fine-tuning is performed on the training set of ProteinQA.

findings.required_change: Add a source-supported split/selection boundary identifying the training subset used by the alignment route, while preserving validation and test branches if represented.

findings.detail: PubMedQA and MedMCQA are collapsed into one biomedical_qa_examples node and one opaque input boundary. Their parallel dataset provenance is therefore lost.

evidence.quote: We fine-tune the language model of BioMedGPT-10B on the training sets of PubMedQA and MedMCQA which consists of a similar amount of data.

findings.required_change: Represent PubMedQA and MedMCQA as distinct source branches or preserve their provenance explicitly as separate aligned inputs to the language-model fine-tuning boundary.

findings.detail: The biomedical-QA evaluation route combines all three datasets without preserving the documented ID/OOD distinction. PubMedQA and MedMCQA are in-domain test sets, while USMLE is evaluated out of domain without additional fine-tuning.

evidence.quote: Then we perform in-domain (ID) evaluation on the test sets of two datasets, and out-of-domain (OOD) evaluation on USMLE without additional fine-tuning on its training set.

We evaluate BioMedGPT-10B on three public multiple-choice question answering benchmarks within the biomedical domain, i.e., USMLE [Jin et al., 2021], MedMCQA [Pal et al., 2022], and PubMedQA [Jin et al., 2019].

findings.required_change: Split the evaluation input into ID branches for MedMCQA and PubMedQA and an OOD USMLE branch, retaining the no-additional-fine-tuning condition for USMLE.

findings.detail: The pretraining selection step merges S2ORC extraction with later full-text and duplicate filtering. The paper gives these as ordered stages, and the graph also uses refined_biomedical_documents without listing it as an intermediate node.

evidence.quote: We meticulously extract 5.5 million biomedical papers from this dataset using PubMed Central (PMC)-ID and PubMed ID as criteria. After removing articles without full text and those with duplicate IDs, we attain a refined dataset of 4.2 million articles.

findings.required_change: Represent the S2ORC source, biomedical-paper extraction, 5.5-million-paper intermediate, full-text/duplicate filtering, and 4.2-million-paper refined intermediate as ordered stages; declare refined_biomedical_documents in the step's intermediate_nodes.
